items.text: HIX Preview: GROHE SPA to bring a taste of Milan to London • Hotel Designs HIX Preview: GROHE SPA to bring a taste of Milan to London WORDS BY Sienna Shipton November 18, 2026 Atkinson Phillip Jeffries Sanderson ADA Grohe Balsan Harrison Spinks Hypnos Lemi Schulter Soho Lighting WISA Zennio HIX Preview: GROHE SPA to bring a taste of Milan to London GROHE returns to HIX 2026 for a sixth consecutive year, bringing a taste of Milan Design Week to ExCeL London with a showcase of premium wellness, aqua technology and bathroom innovation, led by the 3D printed AquaTree… Leading global bathroom brand GROHE will once again take centre stage at HIX 2026 for the sixth consecutive year, the premier hotel design event taking place at Excel London this November. This year’s exhibition theme, ‘Changes’, explores how the industry is rethinking the way spaces are designed, used and experienced. For 2026, GROHE will bring a taste of Milan Design Week to HIX, immersing guests in a unique world of premium wellness, aqua technology and modern bathroom innovation. Working closely with the LIXIL Global Design team, the showcase will display the latest innovations from the premium GROHE SPA sub-brand, alongside new technology and leading design collaborations. Visitors will be invited to experience the GROHE SPA brand first hand, through working demonstrations and tactile displays, highlighting the brand’s commitment to design excellence, innovation and conscious water use. Image credit: GROHE At the heart of the showcase will be GROHE SPA’s latest developments across showers, taps, accessories, and fittings. The showcase focal point will be GROHE SPA’s innovative AquaTree; a 3D printed showering masterpiece that reimagines bathroom fittings to inspire and create emotional connection. Elsewhere, new launches will be on display such as the new Allure Gravity customisable taps with Caesarstone inlets, and the new Grohtherm Aqua Tiles showers will also feature, to highlight GROHE SPA’s approach to combining distinctive design with a more immersive bathroom experience across all touch points. The showcase will also spotlight GROHE SPA’s collaboration with premium functional fittings brand, Buster + Punch, bringing together GROHE’s expertise in premium bathroom design with Buster + Punch’s distinctive approach to materials, finishes and detailing. The collaboration offers a fresh perspective on the contemporary bathroom, where fittings are increasingly considered as part of the wider interior. Technology will also take centre stage, with working displays of GROHE’s new AquaBooster shower technology. Visitors will be able to experience how it enhances the showering experience, delivering a powerful, satisfying spray while using water more consciously. GROHE can be found at stand E70 at HIX on 25th and 26th November 2026. GROHE is one of our Recommended Suppliers and regularly features in our Supplier News section of the website. items.title: Off-grid luxury in Anantara Tented Camp Kafue River
items.summary:
Hotel Designs  
 Off-grid luxury in Anantara Tented Camp Kafue River  
  Off-grid luxury in Anantara Tented Camp Kafue River  
 Pauline Brettell .
items.text: Off-grid luxury in Anantara Tented Camp Kafue River • Hotel Designs Off-grid luxury in Anantara Tented Camp Kafue River WORDS BY Pauline Brettell November 18, 2026 Atkinson Phillip Jeffries Sanderson ADA Grohe Balsan Harrison Spinks Hypnos Lemi Schulter Soho Lighting WISA Zennio Off-grid luxury in Anantara Tented Camp Kafue River Three years in the making, Anantara has unveiled Anantara Tented Camp Kafue River, its first safari property in Africa, in the same year the brand celebrates its 25th anniversary… The intimate 13‑key Anantara Tented Camp Kafue River , embodies African modernism through clean lines, materials shaped by hand and landscape‑informed design, forming an off‑the‑grid sanctuary on the Kafue River in Zambia’s largest national park. By placing wellness on equal footing with conservation‑focused safari experiences developed in partnership with African Parks, the lodge reshapes expectations of what a modern safari experience can offer. Image credit: Anantara Hotels & Resorts Travellers are rewarded with absolute seclusion and a slower rhythm on the banks of one of the country’s most vital waterways. The only lodge in Zambia elevated 3.5 metres above the ground, Anantara Kafue is set on rosewood platforms to protect essential wildlife corridors, with private river frontage offering uninterrupted views of a thriving wilderness where hippos, elephants, large predators, antelope and more than 500 bird species flourish. Kafue National Park, one of Africa’s least explored wildernesses, is entering a new phase of renewal through African Parks’ partnership with the Government of Zambia. Since 2022, strengthened security, rebuilt infrastructure and improved fire management have laid the foundations for wildlife to return across its 22,480 km² expanse. These efforts have enabled landmark restoration milestones, from the reintroduction of Kafue lechwe antelope in 2024 to Zambia’s largest wildlife translocation in 2025, which brought wildebeest and zebra back to long‑quiet grasslands. For Anantara Kafue guests, the park’s transformation into a thriving, resilient ecosystem becomes an essential part of the experience. Image credit: Anantara Hotels & Resorts Designed by Meg Ralph Spaces and honoured with top LIV Hospitality Design Awards, the camp embraces a contemporary, light‑footprint, running on solar power with on‑site water purification and minimal single‑use plastics. Charcoal and canvas exteriors echo the tones of the bush, while sculpted wood and natural textiles reflect Zambia’s beauty and cultural heritage. Structures are built around large riverine trees, such as Marulas and Jackalberries. Spacious suites positioned for horizon‑wide views and calming interiors are shaped by natural materials and organic curves and colours such as olive green, terracotta and cobalt blue, taken from the landscape. Image credit: Anantara Hotels & Resorts The camp’s signature feature, the three 110‑square‑metre Horizon Terrace Suites, are suspended 14.3 metres above the ground and accessed by a glass elevator that dissolves into the landscape. The upper deck is dedicated to open‑air living, with a star bed for sleepouts beneath the night sky. Below, an oversized private terrace extends the experience with uninterrupted sunrise‑to‑sunset views. With ample room for massages on both floors and a design that elevates outlook, Horizon Terrace Suites marry high‑altitude safari with bespoke wellness. Image credit: Anantara Hotels & Resorts Nine 115‑square‑metre Pool and Bush Villas rise 3.5 metres above the ground on timber platforms, each one a grand tented sanctuary immersed in the landscape. Heated plunge pools overlook the river, while an indoor massage room with sweeping river views anchors the villa’s wellness focus. At 400 square metres, the spacious Presidential Villa is designed for poolside entertaining and relaxation 3.5 metres over the river, complete with a dedicated indoor massage zone, exclusive boat access and mature trees shading a spacious deck. Dedicated villa hosts are on hand for bespoke meals, activities, spa bookings as there is no set schedule here. Image credit: Anantara Hotels & Resorts At Anantara Kafue, meals are included as part of the stay, with guests free to dine at the venue that suits their mood. As part of the brand’s signature Designer Dining experience, a floating platform anchored gently into the river hosts intimate breakfasts, afternoon tea and sunset wine tasting. Seating up to four guests who arrive by boat, the slick wooden pontoon sits almost at water level. Its sunken central lounge, reminiscent of a conversation pit, creates a cocooned space for dining, stargazing and unobtrusive wildlife observation as crocodiles and hippos bask along the shores. Other dining experiences celebrate the gastronomic richness of Zambia, from Luzuba Harvestry’s modern classics beneath a canopy of trees to Twalumba Bar & Lounge, where guests return from safari to afternoon tea, signature cocktails and fireside storytelling. Image credit: Anantara Hotels & Resorts Wellness, a core part of the Anantara Kafue experience, is shaped by nature, from birdwatching and stargazing to laps in the full‑size pool. The one-of-a-kind floating Technogym fitness platform is anchored on the river with sliding doors that open directly to the landscape, an outdoor deck for yoga and a wooden swing positioned in a quiet spot facing the water. Anantara Spa treatments, from couples’ rituals and signature massages to local therapies, can be enjoyed in the seclusion of a massage room in each suite or villa, followed by the in‑room steam shower. It’s a rare distinction that makes Anantara Kafue the only property in Zambia to offer such an experience. items.text: Starwood Hotels announces new General Managers at 1 Hotel Melbourne and 1 Hotel Toronto • Hotel Designs Starwood Hotels announces new General Managers at 1 Hotel Melbourne and 1 Hotel Toronto WORDS BY Pauline Brettell November 17, 2026 Atkinson Phillip Jeffries Sanderson ADA Grohe Balsan Harrison Spinks Hypnos Lemi Schulter Soho Lighting WISA Zennio Starwood Hotels announces new General Managers at 1 Hotel Melbourne and 1 Hotel Toronto Starwood Hotels, hotel brand management company operating Baccarat Hotels, 1 Hotels, and Treehouse Hotels, has announced the appointments of Anthony Campaniaris as General Manager of 1 Hotel Melbourne and Jean-Philip Dupré as General Manager of 1 Hotel Toronto… Campaniaris, who previously served as General Manager of 1 Hotel Toronto , will take on his new role in Melbourne , while Dupré joins the brand following his tenure as General Manager of Le Germain Hotel Toronto Mercer. The appointments bring proven expertise across luxury, lifestyle, and boutique hospitality to both properties, reinforcing 1 Hotels’ commitment to exceptional guest experiences, strong team cultures, and meaningful connections with local communities. 1 Hotel Melbourne | Image credit: Mikkel Vang Anthony Campaniaris | Image credit: Starwood “Anthony and Jean-Philip are both accomplished leaders who understand the importance of building strong teams and creating meaningful connections with guests and local communities,” commented Starwood Hotels CEO Raul Leal. “Anthony has been an integral part of the 1 Hotels team in Toronto, and we’re excited to see him take on this next chapter in Melbourne. Jean-Philip’s knowledge of Toronto’s hospitality landscape and people-first approach make him a natural fit to lead 1 Hotel Toronto. We’re confident both will continue to build on the success of these properties.” With more than 20 years in luxury and lifestyle hospitality, Campaniaris has built a career spanning hotel operations, team leadership, and business development. In his new role, he will oversee all aspects of operations at 1 Hotel Melbourne, with a focus on operational performance, the hotel’s food and beverage and wellness offerings, and its continued growth within Melbourne’s luxury hospitality market. Opened in June 2025 along the Yarra River, the 277-room property marked 1 Hotels’ debut in Australia and has since earned a MICHELIN Key. Campaniaris joins 1 Hotel Melbourne from 1 Hotel Toronto, where he served as General Manager since 2023, overseeing all aspects of hotel operations, including the property’s four dining venues. During his tenure, he helped strengthen the hotel’s operational performance and establish its position within Toronto’s competitive luxury hospitality market. “I’m excited to continue my journey with 1 Hotels in Melbourne, a city known for its incredible food, arts, and culture,” said Campaniaris. “I look forward to working alongside the team to build on the hotel’s success and strengthen its connection to the local community.” Prior to joining 1 Hotels, Campaniaris held leadership positions at several of Toronto’s leading luxury hotels, including Director of Hotel Operations at The Hazelton Hotel and Director of Sales and Business Development at Shangri-La Toronto. He also played a key role in the opening of The Anndore House and held international responsibilities with Nobu Hospitality, contributing to hotel projects in Warsaw and Atlanta. Jean-Philip Dupré | Image credit: Brandon Barre / Starwood Having held leadership roles across luxury, lifestyle, and boutique hotels in Canada, Dupré brings a strong background in hotel operations, team development, and food and beverage. In his new role, he will oversee all aspects of operations at 1 Hotel Toronto, with a focus on driving operational excellence, supporting the hotel’s culinary programming, and fostering a strong team culture. Located in the city’s King West neighborhood, the nature-inspired luxury hotel is known for its thoughtfully designed accommodations, distinctive dining venues, and community-driven guest programming. Dupré joins 1 Hotel Toronto following his role as General Manager of Le Germain Hotel Toronto Mercer, where he led initiatives to elevate the guest experience, expand the property’s culinary offerings, and strengthen relationships within the local community. During his tenure, the hotel’s signature restaurant, PUNCH, was recognized in Toronto Life’s Best New Restaurants of 2026 and selected for inclusion in the MICHELIN Guide. “I’m thrilled to join 1 Hotel Toronto and become part of a brand that shares my belief in authentic hospitality and meaningful human connection,” said Dupré. “I look forward to working alongside the team to build on the hotel’s success and create memorable experiences that celebrate the people, culture, and creativity of Toronto.” Throughout his career, Dupré has held leadership positions with Germain Hotels, Hyatt, and Loews Hotels across Winnipeg, Ottawa, Montréal, and Toronto. Appointed to his first General Manager position at just 27 years old, he has developed a leadership approach centered on authenticity, inclusivity, and organizational culture. He also serves on the Board of Directors of the Greater Toronto Hotel Association, contributing to industry advocacy and the continued development of Toronto as a leading hospitality destination. Originally from Ottawa, Dupré spent much of his early life in Montréal, where he began his hospitality career. He holds a Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Relations from the Université de Montréal and is fluent in English and French. 1 Hotel Melbourne | Main image credit: Mikkel Vang You might also like Treehouse puts down roots in Adelaide News / 20.11.2026 Shangri-La Group Appoints Hakan Ozel as Vice President, Operations for London, Paris and Istanbul New Appointment / 19.10.2026 Nijad Fares appointed General Manager of 1 Hotel Seattle New Appoitnment / 01.10.2026 SPACE: the latest issue In video Latest articles Product

items.title: The transformation of Elysée New York
items.summary:
Hotel Designs  
 The transformation of Elysée New York  
  The transformation of Elysée New York  
 Pauline Brettell .
items.text: The transformation of Elysée New York • Hotel Designs The transformation of Elysée New York WORDS BY Pauline Brettell November 17, 2026 Atkinson Phillip Jeffries Sanderson ADA Grohe Balsan Harrison Spinks Hypnos Lemi Schulter Soho Lighting WISA Zennio The transformation of Elysée New York Elysée New York has announced its reopening following a complete transformation, entering its next century of hospitality – the Midtown Manhattan landmark will debut as the flagship property of Wunderkind Hotels & Resorts… A true New York institution since it first opened in 1926, Elysée New York enters a new era as the flagship property of Wunderkind Hotels & Resorts, a global collection of one-of-a-kind hotels created by Hera Hospitality Group under the creative leadership of legendary designer and art collector Wolfgang Joop, together with his partner and Creative Director Edwin Lemberg. Image credit: Elysée New York A New Chapter for a New York Icon For a century, Elysée New York has occupied a singular place within the cultural fabric of Manhattan . Born during the Roaring Twenties, a defining era of creativity and social change, the hotel became a discreet refuge for artists, writers, actors, and luminaries, defined by its residential character and a spirit of glamour and mischief. Over the decades, its guestrooms welcomed an extraordinary cast of names including Marlon Brando, Tennessee Williams, Maria Callas, Tallulah Bankhead, Helen Hayes, and Jimi Hendrix, cementing Elysée New York’s place as one of Manhattan’s most storied addresses and setting the stage for its next chapter of reinvention. Following an 18-month transformation and for its 100th anniversary, Elysée New York will emerge as an 83-key hotel that honors the soul and heritage of its first century while introducing a contemporary expression of hospitality. A proud member of The Leading Hotels of the World, the hotel has been reimagined through Wolfgang Joop’s and Edwin Lemberg’s distinctive creative lens, inspired by his eclectic world of art and design. The transformation brings together art, craftsmanship, and interiors to create a new interpretation of Elysée New York. Image credit: Elysée New York A Legacy of Gathering and Celebration At the heart of Elysée New York’s social legacy, Monkey Bar will remain an integral part of the hotel’s experience. A fixture of Manhattan’s dining scene for nearly 90 years, the restaurant continues to celebrate its singular personality through its iconic monkey murals by caricaturist Charlie Wala. The monkey motif also informs the identity of Elysée New York and Wunderkind Hotels & Resorts, inspired by Wolfgang Joop’s childhood memories of Sanssouci Palace in Potsdam, Germany. Its name, derived from the French for “without worries,” has long symbolized beauty, freedom, and the art of living. On the second floor, Salon Sanssouci, named in homage to the palace, will introduce a new gathering place centered around the art of everyday moments, refined indulgence, and lingering conversation. Image credit: Elysée New York Residential Luxury Reimagined Elysée New York’s 83 guestrooms and suites have been redesigned to offer a refined interpretation of residential luxury. Elysée New York’s culinary offerings will include Salon Sanssouci, under the direction of acclaimed Austrian chef Eduard Frauneder, complemented by a curated wine selection from Wölffer Estate Vineyard in the Hamptons. The hotel will also offer guests access to an exclusive partnership with medical and longevity experts Hamptons BioMed, featuring a curated collection of signature treatments for facial and body rejuvenation, as well as New York City’s only Human Regenerator, located just moments from the hotel. Further details about the hotel’s design transformation will be revealed ahead of opening. “Elysée New York is a character shaped by a century of New York mythology,” said Wolfgang Joop, Co-Founder of Hera Hospitality Group. “I do not decorate a building like that – I listen to it, and then I answer. Our goal was never simply to restore a historic hotel, but to honor its past while expressing my own stylistic identity in every decision we made. New York has always held a special place in my creative journey, and the Elysée felt like the natural home for Wunderkind’s first hotel because it embodies the elegance, warmth, trust and authenticity that define the brand.” The Debut of Wunderkind Hotels & Resorts The reopening of Elysée New York marks the debut of Wunderkind Hotels & Resorts, a global collection of one-of-a-kind boutique hotels where creativity, design, and storytelling become a lived experience. Each Wunderkind property will be conceived as a singular expression of its destination, celebrating a strong sense of place and an uncompromising approach to hospitality. “We created Wunderkind Hotels & Resorts to offer a new approach to boutique luxury, shaped by art, craft, and atmosphere,” said Daniel Schneider, Chairman of the Board of Hera Hospitality Group. “Wunderkind is for design-fluent, culturally curious travelers who value character and creative energy over convention. With Elysée New York, we are bringing that vision to life for the first time, pairing the spirit of a storied New York landmark with a bold new chapter in its history. It is an exciting beginning for Wunderkind Hotels & Resorts and for Hera Hospitality Group.” Main image credit: Elysée New York You might also like Miniview: 1898 Porter’s house – an intimate luxury retreat Hotel Design / 12.11.2026 In conversation with: Paul Glade – the Creative Director behind Fowlescombe Farm In conversation / 22.10.2026 360 Hotel – rooted in Icelandic heritage News / 14.10.2026 SPACE: the latest issue In video Latest articles Product watch: Xuniva Evo from hansgrohe sets the tone in the bathroom 23.11.2026 Minor Hotels appoints Karin Kopano as Managing Director of The Wolseley Hotel New York 23.11.2026 Mama Shelter Mexico City – a vibrant collision of design 20.11.202

The 19 winners awarded at the ninth annual Dezeen Awards ceremony are located in 11 different countries, including […]

items.text: Chater Paul Jordan 16 November 2026 A tree-top sauna that punctures its architectural framework with the surrounding woodland has been named Dezeen Awards 2026 architecture project of the year following the announcement of all 19 architecture category winners at a party in London. The 19 winners awarded at the ninth annual Dezeen Awards ceremony are located in 11 different countries, including Canada , France , India , Japan and Mexico . Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna won the project of the year award in the architecture sector, it was also named leisure and wellness project of the year. Leisure and wellness projects win big again The judges hailed the biophilic project as “beautifully minimalist with a spiritual touch of the soul”. “It’s totally fresh, totally innovative, and never seen before,” they added. The win marks the second consecutive year that the leisure and wellness project of the year has gone on to claim the overall sector title, following Herzog & de Meuron’s win last year . Architecture project of the year announced Silent River Tree Sauna by Daichi Previous Next The winning project of the year was up against category winners including a sprawling brick-clad university building modelled on stepped wells in India, a country house with walls formed of unstabilised rammed earth in the UK and a project featuring an 18-kilometre-long limestone wall that allows wildlife to pass through in Mexico. A housing project that appears as if emerging from the natural landscape and a viewpoint designed to evoke a giant silver ring left on the burial site of a legendary Viking were also amongst the category winners. Read more about all the winning architecture projects below: Photos by Daichi Architecture project of the year and leisure and wellness project of the year: Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna by Daichi The project is nestled within a forest in Kanagawa, southwest of Tokyo , and forms part of the Daichi Silent River retreat alongside guest cabins and additional sauna spaces. Leisure and wellness is also about mental health, which this project addresses perfectly The idea for the project was to make the trees feel part of the architecture, using them as both supports and the defining feature of the pared-back structure. “Leisure and wellness is also about mental health, which this project addresses perfectly,” said the master jury. “It is a building that offers a spiritual connection between humans and nature.” Read more about Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna Photos by Toshihisa Ishii House (urban) project of the year: Amami House by Sakai Architects Local studio Sakai Architects won urban house of the year for its off-grid home on Amami Ōshima, an island in the Amami archipelago off Japan ‘s southern coast. This house shows how we can live sustainably on a small footprint, in close relationship to nature The design was informed by the region’s traditional materials and crafts and its development was spurred by the increase in extreme weather conditions on the island. “This house shows how we can live sustainably on a small footprint, in close relationship to nature,” the master jury said. “In a time of climate crisis , it offers an excellent solution for autonomy of energy, while smartly reinterpreting the arrangement and materials of a traditional Japanese house.” Read more about Amami House Photos by Lv Xiaobin House (rural) project of the year: Jiang Deng Lu by Shisuo Design Office Shisuo Design Office won rural house of the year for Jiang Deng Lu in Anhui, China . This project sits very delicately in its context and is beautiful as a result The compact building is raised partially on stilts to look as though it is floating above its sloped riverside site and made using stainless-steel offcuts salvaged from the client’s own factory. “This project sits very delicately in its context and is beautiful as a result,” said the judges. “Innovative in its use of available materials, the project is highly resolved, with incredible quality of light and generosity of space despite a small footprint.” Read more about Jiang Deng Lu Photos by Pepo Vazquez Cortes Housing project of the year: La Querola by Ribas & Ribas Arquitectos Ribas & Ribas Arquitectos won housing project of the year for La Querola in Ordino, Andorra. A deliberate provocation against the salami-type housing where repetition is at the core. Made up of seven irregularly shaped blocks embedded into the sloping valley and clad in locally sourced slate, the building’s facades feature recessed windows and openings revealing outdoor terraces . The judges commended the development’s trend-bucking design as a “deliberately expressionist project, celebrating forms that are not repeatable”. “It’s a deliberate provocation against the salami-type housing where repetition is at the core. It’s unconventional, unique, controversial, and a very strong statement,” they said. Recently, a fire damaged all seven buildings in the uninhabited development. The project also won its category for the 2026 public vote. Read more about La Querola Photos by Shinya Sato House renovation of the year: Haniyasu House by Aatismo Local architecture studio Aatismo won house renovation of the year for Haniyasu House, a home in the coastal town of Kamakura, Japan. It is aesthetic but also functional, cleverly improving seismic stability The project saw the single-storey home, originally built in 1967, stripped back to its timber frame after a typhoon had left it structurally unsound, and boldly characterised with rough walls streaked with clay, soil and metal powders to evoke ceramic glazes. The judges praised the project’s sensitivity to “the history of both the architecture and its owners”. “It is aesthetic but also functional, cleverly improving seismic stability,” they added. items.summary:

The 14 winners awarded in Dezeen’s annual awards programme are located in 10 different countries, including Australia, China, Czech Republic, […] 
 The post  Dezeen Awards 2026 interiors project of the year announced  appeared first on  Dezeen .
items.text: Chater Paul Jordan 16 November 2026 An old sailor’s home that pays homage to its nautical heritage has won Dezeen Awards 2026 interiors project of the year following the announcement of all 14 interiors category winners at a party in London. The 14 winners awarded in Dezeen’s annual awards programme are located in 10 different countries, including Australia , China , Czech Republic , Kazakhstan , Mexico and Ukraine . La Casa del Pirata by Raul Sanchez Architects won the interiors project of the year award, sponsored by Gaggenau . It was also named residential interior (small) project of the year. “This was probably the boldest and most well-executed project we saw,” said the judges. “They kept everything that was already there and made a much more interesting place,” adding that, “it’s very well-thought-out in terms of how space has been used.” Interiors project of the year revealed La Casa del Pirata by Raul Sanchez Architects Previous Next The winning project of the year was up against category winners, including a restaurant that features “direct and unrefined” materials to create tactile interior in Canada, a pink stepped-facade-fronted commercial building and interiors in Mexico and a boutique that recalls a traditional yurt in Kazakhstan. A boutique hotel in Bali focused on playful spaces and Indonesian music and culture and a warehouse into a workspace divided by glass partitions and filled with design classics, including an entire Jean Prouvé house were also amongst the category winners. Read more about all the winning interiors projects below: Interiors project of the year and residential interior (small) of the year: La Casa del Pirata by Raul Sanchez Architects The Spanish practice renovated the home in Mataro, Spain , which belonged to a sailor in the 19th century, updating its interiors to suit the lifestyle of his descendant, who lives there now. There was no discussion – this was the winner The project saw the renovation of three spaces: the entrance hall, the dining room and the living area. The judges praised the project’s bold approach, noting there was no deliberation over its winning credentials: “There was no discussion – this was the winner.” “It’s super unusual,” they continued, “and we liked to see an intervention in a very historical space where they decided to not play it safe.” Read more about La Casa del Pirata Residential interior (large) of the year: Garden Home by Gisbert Pöppler Local studio Gisbert Pöppler won residential interior (large) of the year for its renovation of a 1920s villa in Ruhr, Germany . For this project, we were swayed by the colours and use of materials, as well as the contrast between the very classic exterior of the house and its interior The interior design features a bold colour scheme and artisanal details that reflect its association with the Deutscher Werkbund movement, which caught the judges’ eyes. “For this project, we were swayed by the colours and use of materials, as well as the contrast between the very classic exterior of the house and its interior,” they said. “It has character and doesn’t play it safe,” they continued. Read more about Garden Home Restaurant interior of the year: Jeju by &Daughters Canadian studio &Daughters won restaurant interior of the year for Jeju, a Korean restaurant in Vancouver , Canada. This project has a level of innovation while being quite exquisite in every element A rich material palette of basalt, cork, concrete, thatch and wood characterises the restaurant interior, which nods to traditional touches in its contemporary design. “This project has a level of innovation while being quite exquisite in every element,” the master jury said. “It’s contemporary and still a bit traditional. There’s also a cultural influence that’s being used well and isn’t just there for decoration.” The project also won its category for the 2026 public vote. Read more about Jeju Bar and cafe interior of the year: Laibei 1087 by Tan t A Temps Design Laibei 1087 by Tant A Temps Design in Xi’an, China, won bar and cafe interior of the year, sponsored by Programa . There are a lot of beautiful projects, but this one is really refreshing – it’s working with the building, but also reinventing it Located inside the Beilin Museum, the cafe’s interior aimed to revive the aesthetics of the Tang Dynasty and used a minimal intervention renovation strategy with every new addition detachable and reversible, which allowed the building’s original features to remain untouched. “This project is new and modern, but still connected to the past,” the judges said. “There are a lot of beautiful projects, but this one is really refreshing – it’s working with the building, but also reinventing it.” “The architect has taken symbolic elements and simplified them, which makes it feel quite fresh.” Read more about Laibei 1087 Hotel and short-stay interior of the year: Moon Gang by YSG Studio Australian studio YSG won hotel and short-stay interior of the year for its conversion of a former private vacation residence into a boutique hotel in Bali , Indonesia. There’s a lot of innovation and playfulness here, and a good use of local craftsmanship, as well as a collaborative spirit Focused on playful spaces and Indonesian music and culture, Moon Gang Bali hotel is located among the rice fields on the northern outskirts of Ubud and includes five interconnected suites, outdoor terraces and a lounge surrounding a central courtyard. YSG was influenced by Indonesian and Japanese design for the hotel’s spaces, which feature bamboo and timber structures and lava stone tiling. “There’s a lot of innovation and playfulness here, and a good use of local craftsmanship, as well as a collaborative spirit,” commended the master jury. items.text: Dezeen Awards 27 October 2026 The results of the interiors public vote for Dezeen Awards 2026 have been announced, with 14 projects selected as winners by Dezeen’s readers. Projects voted as readers’ favourite include a co-working space in Berlin that offers “more than a boring desk” , as well as a “quietly magical” Toronto cafe that provides a family-friendly third place . Also winning this year’s public vote is an office in Kyiv featuring vintage furnishings, artworks, and quirky touches such as leftover paint swatches . Dezeen Awards 2026 public vote winners revealed this week Dezeen Awards 2026, in partnership with Trimble , will reveal all public vote winners this week. The architecture winners were announced yesterday and the design winners will be revealed tomorrow. Readers were invited to choose their favourite projects out of the 392-strong shortlist in this year’s vote. The vote took place between 28 September and 16 October, spanning shortlists in each of Dezeen Awards’ three main category sectors. This year’s interiors category sponsors include Framery and Programa . Top: Banda Agency Office by Ater Architects. Photo by Yevhenii Avramenko. Above: Coworking Spaces at C1 Alexanderplatz-Berlin by Bruzkus Greenberg. Photo by Bruzkus Greenberg All winning interiors projects are listed below, each with a link to a dedicated page on the Dezeen Awards website where you can find an image and more information about the project. items.summary:
This week on Dezeen, we revealed the architecture, interiors and design projects in the running to win this year's Dezeen Awards. items.text: Tom Ravenscroft Editor-in-chief 26 September 2026 This week on Dezeen , we revealed the architecture, interiors and design projects in the running to win this year’s Dezeen Awards . Over the week, we announced all the projects shortlisted for this year’s awards, starting with the 152 projects in the running for the 19 architecture project categories on Monday . On Tuesday, we revealed the 112 shortlisted projects in the 14 different interiors project categories before unveiling the shortlisted design projects on Wednesday. Bentley revealed its first electric car this week In London, car brand Bentley revealed its first fully electric car – an SUV named the Torcal. Ahead of its unveiling, we spoke to design director Robin Page about how the car aims to embrace heritage in a “progressive way”. Bugatti unveiled plans for a skyscraper in Miami In the USA, car brand Bugatti revealed plans to build a 60-storey skyscraper in Miami , which would be its first branded residence in the US. Designed by US architecture studio Brandon Haw Architecture with interiors by Yabu Pushelberg , the skyscraper would join other developments by luxury car brands Porsche , Bentley , Mercedes-Benz and Aston Martin in the city. Meta showcased its Muse Charm device At the Meta Connect showcase, the tech company revealed a series of new products including two new pairs of smart glasses . The company also debuted its Muse Charm device , which is a tamagotchi-style AI agent. “We’ve packed a lot of technology into this little guy,” said Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg. “So if you’re not wearing glasses, this is going to be by far the fastest way to talk to your Muse and to show it what’s going on around you.” A Peter Zumthor gallery was one of this week’s most popular projects The most popular projects on Dezeen this week include a trio of buildings for a Swiss museum by Peter Zumthor , a charred timber-clad home in Japan , a multi-generational house in Bengaluru . Listen to our journalists talk about the key design and architecture stories of the past seven days on our Dezeen Weekly podcast , which this week focused on Apple’s folding phone. This week on Dezeen This week on Dezeen is our regular roundup of the week’s top news stories. Subscribe to our newsletters to be sure you don’t miss anything. items.text: Dezeen Awards 24 September 2026 Dezeen Awards, in partnership with Trimble , teamed up with content creator Reece Davey to ask this year’s master jury where the future of architecture and design is headed, in this video . In the reel, the jury members (pictured above) were asked for one thing about the future of architecture or design that excited them, as well as trends spotted from this year’s entries. Davey spoke to architects Daniel Libeskind and Aziza Chaouni , as well as architectural designer John Cummins . He also heard from interior designers Jaime Hayon , Julien Sebban and Smita Thomas , alongside designers Jo Barnard and Martin Lotti . View this post on Instagram A post shared by Reece Davey (@houseofdvey) Reece Davey questioned the Dezeen Awards master jury on the future of design and architecture The jury also discussed how representing ideas, sketching, modelling and visualising are changing and the way in which designers work today. For Cummins, product marketing manager at 3D modelling software company Trimble SketchUp , the value of software lies in how easily it allows a designer to move between different stages of a project, from an initial idea to a three-dimensional model and eventually a finished building. “Software should not be another problem that the designer has to solve,” said Cummins. “SketchUp has always been about giving architects the tools to seamlessly take a project from an idea to a finished building,” he later added. The jury met earlier this month at the One Hundred Shoreditch hotel in London to decide the winners of Dezeen Awards 2026, which will be revealed at this year’s party on 16 November. items.summary:

items.text: Chater Paul Jordan 17 September 2026 Fifteen leading architects and designers met last week to decide the winners of Dezeen Awards 2026, in partnership with Trimble , which will be revealed at the Dezeen Awards 2026 party in November. The master jury took place at the One Hundred Shoreditch hotel in London and included architects Ma Yansong and Daniel Libeskind as well as interior designers Wendy Saunders and Jaime Hayon . Designers Martin Lotti and Jo Barnard , as well as architects Dominique Petit-Frère and Aziza Chaouni also joined to determine the 49 winning projects, ahead of next week’s shortlist announcements between 21-23 September. Winners announced at the Royal Opera House All this year’s winners will be announced at the Dezeen Awards 2026 party which takes place at the Royal Opera House in London on 16 November. Guests at the party will be the first to find out who has won the prestigious project of the year awards across architecture, interiors and design. Tickets are available to purchase here . Also unveiled at the ceremony will be the six winners of this year’s Designers of the Year, who have each been shortlisted and selected by Dezeen’s editorial team. The Designers of the Year awards recognise the best emerging and established talent whose innovative work has made a notable impact on the industry across architecture, interiors and design. “Designers thinking more critically about context” The master jury discussed 392 shortlisted entries selected from over 4,300 projects in 91 countries around the globe. Architectural designer John Cummins joined the architecture master jury panel which comprised architects Yansong , Libeskind , Chaouni and Petit-Frère . Speaking to Dezeen, Petit-Frère observed how “this year’s projects reflect a generation of designers thinking more critically about context, materiality, technology, and the social impact of what they create”. Top image: (from left to right) John Cummins, Dominique Petit-Frère, Daniel Libeskind, Ma Yansong and Aziza Chaouni. Above: (from left to right) Wendy Saunders, Jaime Hayon, Smita Thomas, Benni Allan and Julien Sebban at the master jury day at One Hundred Shoreditch Hayon and Saunders were joined on the interiors master jury panel by Benni Allan , Julien Sebban and Bangalore-based Smita Thomas . Thomas was also struck by the depth of this year’s entries, which she saw as imbued with a sense of purpose rather than being solely aesthetic exercises. “There were a number of projects that felt more like statements of intent than displays of style,” she said. “It charged me to see design beginning to shapeshift toward strengthening human connection in a time when we need it most,” Thomas continued. Parisian designer Sebban noted the “presence of so many young and emerging studios experimenting with new materials and new ways of thinking”. “The next generation is asking better questions, not just creating better answers” Lotti and Barnard were alongside Michael Anastassiades , Min Chen and Alexie Sommer to decide the winners of the design categories. Lotti, chief design officer at sportswear brand Nike , remarked that “the strongest projects weren’t simply beautiful – they were purposeful, distinct and challenging the status quo”. “What struck me most was the range of thinking behind it. I came away feeling that the next generation is asking better questions, not just creating better answers,” he continued. (From left to right) Alexie Sommer, Min Chen, Michael Anastassiades, Jo Barnard and Martin Lotti at the master jury day in London Following the day of judging, an exclusive drinks reception and dinner took place in the One Hundred Room at One Hundred Shoreditch, where the master jury was joined by fellow 2026 judges Zandra Rhodes and Miminat Shodeinde . Designers Paul Cocksedge , Ron Arad and Sebastian Cox also joined to celebrate the day’s conclusion. Following the shortlist announcements next week, the Dezeen Awards 2026 public vote will open and readers will be asked to vote for their favourite shortlisted projects. We will announce the public vote winners on Dezeen and across our social media channels ahead of the Dezeen Awards party on 16 November. items.text: Chater Paul Jordan 1 June 2026 British architect Norman Foster is the latest industry leader to be announced as a member of the judging panel for Dezeen Awards 2026 . Dezeen Awards, in partnership with Trimble , is searching for the world’s best architecture, interiors and design. The search finally concludes this coming Wednesday, 3 June at 23:59 London time – there will be no extension to the deadline . Read on for more as “the most successful architect in history” joins this year’s panel. Foster to judge Dezeen Awards 2026 Foster, whose career spans nearly six decades, is renowned as one of the industry’s most prolific names. He leads international studio Foster + Partners, which he founded in 1967, and is behind some of the most notable projects in the world. The architect’s oeuvre reflects his impact as a pioneer and proponent of high-tech architecture . Norman Foster will judge Dezeen Awards 2026 Landmark projects include the HSBC Building in Hong Kong , London Stansted Airport and Apple Park, USA . In an interview with Dezeen, Foster expanded on the importance of “architecture without architects” , advocating for the lessons the industry can take from using buildings constructed with local materials and with passive design strategies. Last year, on the eve of his 90th birthday, Dezeen explored how the Manchester-born architect grew to become the most successful architect in history , speaking to former colleagues and industry peers – including Foster himself. Still highly prolific, he remains at the helm of the global architectural powerhouse as executive chairman, while also serving as president of the Norman Foster Foundation – an initiative that promotes interdisciplinary thinking and research to help new generations of architects, designers and urbanists anticipate the future. Recent projects by Foster + Partners include an art gallery wrapped in with ribbed glass facades , a supertall skyscraper in Manhattan and a museum signalled by soaring ventilation towers modelled on the wings of a falcon . Other projects include a bespoke time capsule created to mark the USA’s 250th anniversary of independence . It will be buried under the plaza at Washington Monument and is destined to be reopened on 4th July 2276 for the USA ‘s 500th Independence Day. Foster is the latest judge to be announced as part of this year’s Dezeen Awards judging panel. He will join the architecture panel alongside Daniel Libeskind , Massimiliano Fuksas and Amanda Levete as well as Malini Doshi , Dominique Petit-Frère and Annabelle Selldorf . Final chance to enter Dezeen Awards is accepting late entries until 3 June at 23:59 London time , meaning you have one final week to submit your entries to this year’s edition. items.text: NYC Restaurant News ICYMI: Taqueria Ramirez’s Charcoal-Focused Taco Restaurant Opens in December And more New York City restaurant intel to know this week by Nadia Chaudhury and Melissa McCart Updated Nov 23, 2026, 1:25 AM UTC Facebook Link Luke Fortney We’ve been covering various NYC restaurants, food, drinks, bars, etc. news intel over on our daily newsletter ( please sign up if you haven’t already! ), but we’re also making it easier for everyone to catch up by rounding ‘em up here every week (check out October , September , August , July , and June’s ). November 20 Rapidly growing taqueria opens next spot soon The Taqueria Ramirez team is really on a nonstop expansion tear this year. After opening Socceria and Camron El Peludo, co-owners and chef Giovanni Cervantes and Tania Apolinar are opening a charcoal-grill spinoff , Ramirez al Carbón , in Carroll Gardens on Thursday, December 3, Caper reports . The address is 267 Smith Street, at Degraw Street. — Nadia Chaudhury Big Indian restaurant group shutters in Brooklyn Unapologetic Foods has closed Masalawala & Sons in Park Slope after four years. Sunday, November 15, was its last day of service. The building was sold, and the group is looking for a new, larger location. “The neighborhood has been very good to us, and we are incredibly grateful to all our diners,” the group said in a statement to Eater. The group said they could have stayed but want to expand the brand. — Melissa McCart NYC spots will have to stock naloxone By Sunday, December 13, New York City bars, restaurants, and nightclubs will have to stock naloxone — the opioid reversal medication used in the event of an overdose — as part of their first-aid supplies, Bushwick Daily reports . — NC New dining options for commuters A follow-up supersized restaurant opens in Grand Central: Vizz Group, the team behind Vanderbilt Hall’s 400-seat Grand Brasserie , opened Osteria Centrale (89 E. 42nd Street, at Park Avenue) on Tuesday, November 17, in the terminal’s southwest corner, complete with 250 seats, a 50-seat bar, and a menu of Italian staples. Rockwell Group designed both the restaurant and its neighboring grab-and-go market, Mercato Centrale , drawing on an Italian spritz garden for the vibe. The restaurant’s hours are 11 a.m. to 2 a.m. daily; the self-checkout market will run from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m., stocked with coffee, sandwiches, salads, and prepared foods. — MM Danny Meyer is taking over Loring Place Danny Meyer is on the move, having picked up what had been Dan Kluger’s Loring Place from 2016 until this July. Andrea Strong reports that the lease is signed for 21 West Eighth Street, between Fifth and Sixth avenues, and it’ll be a new concept for Meyer’s Union Square Hospitality Group. No word yet on what that is exactly, a spokesperson confirmed, with a targeted opening date this coming year. — MM A Spain spot is expanding into NYC San Sebastián’s Antonio Bar is headed to 65 Carmine Street, at Bleecker Street, in the former Spunto space in the West Village, the Village Reader reports . West Village native Olmo Schnabel, son of artist and filmmaker Julian Schnabel, is behind the project, which Caper first reported on. Schnabel told Community Board 2’s liquor license committee that the original’s two owners will come to New York to run the pintxos restaurant, with plans for 72 seats at tables and another 28 across two bars. The ground floor will open first, with a basement space tentatively following in September 2027, pending permits. No opening date has been announced. — MM NJ chef is opening an Italian Japanese spot in Manhattan Robbie Felice of Pasta Ramen in Montclair is opening an Italian Japanese restaurant in the former home of L’Accolade at 302 Bleecker Street, between Grove and Barrow streets. The rising star James Beard semifinalist chef (2020) spent his early career at Babbo before opening his own restaurants. The plans call for 35 seats, an eight-seat bar, and 20 seats at nine tables in the backyard. No word yet as to the debut date. — MM NYC star sommelier opens a new online wine shop Sommelier Victoria James, the beverage director and partner of Gracious Hospitality (Cote, Coqadaq, etc.), stepped away from the company’s daily operations over the summer. And now, she announced her next project. She’s opening Anna & Willie , a new online wine shop (with East Village wine shop Convive ), where she’ll feature a selection of wines, plus send out an accompanying newsletter highlighting weekly bottles and the such. People who subscribe for $80 get first dibs on everything. She named it after her two grandmothers, Anna from Piemonte and Willie from Tennessee. — NC Pasta at Swaine’s. David Sherwin November 13 A new sibling-run Brooklyn restaurant Sisters Emily Swaine and Hannah Swaine are opening their Williamsburg Italian neighborhood restaurant this month. Swaine’s is opening on Wednesday, November 18 at 577 Lorimer Street, near Metropolitan Avenue. Emily (who had been the executive chef of Forsythia, a sous chef at Maialino, and worked at Blue Hill at Stone Barns) is dishing up an evening menu of dishes including pizzettes with toppings like clams, parsley, and chile or marinara, sliced garlic, and oregano; pasta like bucatini with royal red shrimp; and roasted vegetables like charred cabbage with green tahini and pistachio. For drinks, look for natural wines and cocktails such as the fig leaf sour and dessert-sounding Nonna’s Chocolate Milk. Hannah is running the restaurant’s private events. Book reservations on Resy . The restaurant will start with dinner service from 5 to 11 p.m. Wednesday through Sunday. — Nadia Chaudhury A Chinatown Hong Kong cafe handover happens soon Longtime Chinatown cha chaan teng M Star set its final day of service for New Year’s Eve on Thursday, December 31, per Flushing Foodie . But don’t worry, the address is going into good hands thanks to chef Lucas Sin . The chef has been operating his hot pop-up Lok Kee this year, and he’s taking o

items.text: NYC Restaurant News Acclaimed Doughnuts From London Are Coming to NYC ﻿Bread Ahead makes its stateside debut on the Upper East Side next month by Nadia Chaudhury Nov 20, 2026, 7:38 PM UTC Facebook Link Bread Ahead Nadia Chaudhury is a born-and-raised New Yorker who is the deputy editor for Eater’s Northeast region and Eater New York, was the former Eater Austin editor for 10 years, and often writes about food and pop culture. NYC’s newest bakery is building on not just one, but two trends that are currently happening in the city. First, it’s part of the new wave of bakeries with strong bread offerings, like Altbau and Brooklyn Granary . And then there’s the rising tide of British imports happening, such as Ambassadors Clubhouse and Straker’s . Now, London-based Bread Ahead is bringing its bakery and baking school to America for the first time in New York City this fall, on the Upper East Side at 1571 Second Avenue, near East 82nd Street. The bakery is opening on Tuesday, December 1, with classes at the school starting on Wednesday, December 2. For Bread Ahead founder Matthew Jones, opening in New York City made sense because so many East Coasters have made the trek across the pond to frequent the London bakeries. “Just looking really at our customer profile in our shops in London, it’s overwhelmingly East Coast Americans,” he tells Eater. The Upper East Side made for a good landing spot because it felt like a neighborhood, with fun attractions like Central Park and the Metropolitan Museum of Art. “We want to build a regular residential customer base,” he adds. Breads at Bread Ahead. Bread Ahead Bread Ahead is best known for its filled doughnuts , including the creme brulee one. Other popular varieties include vanilla custard, raspberry jam, sea-salted caramel, velvet chocolate, and pistachio. “I think the doughnuts are going to be a big thing,” Jones says. “New York has got a huge doughnut culture, but we’re bringing good pastries.” Then there are sourdough breads, pastries, baked goods like brownies, and amaretto biscuits. Jones is proud of the sourdough pizza too, which he calls “quite challenging” to do, being “a U.K. brand bringing sourdough pizza.” They’ll sling 20-inch pies along with slices. “For us to bring that into the New York market is quite a bold move, because you guys are really good at it and quite fussy [about it]. I’m pretty confident we’ve got a great product.” Bread Ahead’s baking school will host workshops where people will learn how to make baked goods like doughnuts, sourdough bread, pizza, bagels, holiday items, and regional cuisines; there’s even a class dedicated to working with New York grains. Typically, in-person classes last for three hours and cost $150. A pepperoni pizza from Bread Ahead. Bread Ahead The classes also show people what Bread Ahead is all about. “It’s a very nice way to bring people into the business,” Jones says. “We are a food experience place; we are an educational facility, but we’re also a nice little neighborhood cafe where you can come and have a croissant and a cup of coffee, quite casual, very simple, and we’re not a fancy place. We’re more about the daily grind of New York.” Jones started Bread Ahead in London at the Borough Market in 2013, and tacked on the baking school component in 2014. The company has grown with bakeries throughout London, as well as in the Middle East, Bangkok, and Manila, with more expansion markets in the works. “Our target audience is those sort of young, dynamic foodie cities where we can do very well there,” Jones says, and calls further NYC and American expansions “inevitable; it’s very much early days, but we’re ready for that.” Ahead of the actual opening, Bread Ahead is hosting what it’s calling a two-day doughnut party, in which the bakery will sell its doughnuts and coffee on Saturday, November 28, through Sunday, November 29. Bread Ahead’s scheduled NYC hours will run from 7:30 a.m. to 7 p.m., Tuesday through Sunday. items.text: NYC Restaurant News NYC’s Once-Booming Southern Chain Sweet Chick Falls Flat Plus, a handful of coffee shop shutters — and more closings by Tierney Plumb Updated Nov 20, 2026, 4:40 PM UTC Facebook Link Sweet Chick shut down all of its NYC locations this week. Sweet Chick Tierney Plumb is an editor of Eater’s Northeast region, covering D.C., Boston, Philly, and New York. This is Eater’s guide to all the New York City restaurants, bars, and cafes that closed in November 2026. This list will be updated weekly (see: October , September , August , July , June , May , April , March , February , January ), serving as a round-up of the dining and drinking places that have shuttered around the city. If a restaurant or bar has closed in your neighborhood, let us know at ny@eater.com. November 20 Spotlight Multiple locations: Sweet Chick , NYC’s fast-expanding Southern spot for shrimp and grits, crawfish hush puppies, chicken and waffles, French toast, whiskey cocktails, and daily brunch since 2013, announced its complete chain-wide shutdown on Thursday, November 19. Sweet Chick’s rapid decline started this summer, when the Williamsburg flagship suddenly closed along with its Lower East Side locale. Its last remaining locations in Union Square and Prospect Heights officially closed this week, too. Rapper Nas was an early backer of the brand that expanded at some point all the way to Los Angeles and London. “We thank you all for the years of support and the countless meals & memories we’ve all shared,” the team wrote on Instagram . And the rest… Astoria : Petey’s Burger , whose namesake founder brought his SoCal college love for In-N-Out Burger back to his native NYC in 2008, closed its original Astoria location this week. Petey’s, however, will keep serving its burgers in Queens via a new takeout and delivery collaboration with Sanford’s Restaurant & Whisky Bar. Its Long Island City location remains open with its West Coast-style burgers, shakes, and fries. 30-17 30th Avenue, near 31st Street, Queens Brooklyn: Adesso Bakeshop , the roving Brooklyn pop-up best known for its 12-inch sourdough chocolate chip cookies, will sell its goods for the last time this weekend after two years. Its last market appearances will be held at Fort Greene Park Artisan Bazar on Saturday, November 21, and at Carroll Gardens restaurant Sociale on Sunday, November 22. “This model just isn’t sustainable for us,” per a closing statement. Almond amaretti and mochi brownies were also big draws. Multiple locations Post used biscuits as building blocks for much of its sandwiches. Post East Village: Post , the brunch standard-bearer best known for its flaky biscuit sandwiches, pancakes, and bottled Bon Merde hot sauce, closed after its last Sunday service on November 15. Dinnertime orders included steak frites, croquettes, seared salmon, and vegan burgers. 317 E. Third St., between Avenue B and Avenue C East Village : Bananas , the playful destination for Asian American mashups like chopped cheese krapow, dynamite fried rice, and karaage and no shortage of pop-art nods to its namesake, closed on Sunday, November 15. Chef-owners Chris Ng and Kyaw Lwin opened here in early 2025. 174 First Avenue, near East 11th Street Greenpoint : Pueblo Querido , Brooklyn’s mini java chain fueled on Colombian beans, closed its five-year-old Greenpoint location on Sunday, November 15, with founder Guzman Herrera telling Greenpointers he’s handed the keys to fast-casual Banana King out of New Jersey. The decade-old original remains on Greenpoint Avenue, as do follow-up locations in Williamsburg, Long Island City, and 1 Bell Slip. 698 Manhattan Avenue, near Norman Avenue, Brooklyn Flushing : Carnation Bakery , the family-owned Cantonese walk-in for chicken sandwiches, pineapple buns, and other affordable pastries, closed in November, flags Flushing Foodie . 46-05 Kissena Boulevard, near Holly Avenue, Queens Greenpoint : After three tries of doing a different vegan venture in the same site, the owners of Sotteatery finally threw in the towel in early November. Blenll Mena and Javier Saba originally opened the Brooklyn space as Next Stop Vegan, later to be reinvented as Vegan Quick Bites. The slim setup styled with a thatched tiki look and a leafy back patio most recently transitioned into Sotte earlier this year, focusing on coastal seafood with an ongoing knack for dairy-free ingredients. “We kept reimagining the space because we believed in what we were creating and wanted to give it every opportunity to succeed,” the duo told Greenpointers . “We put a great deal of heart, time, and effort into making this location work. Ultimately, despite those efforts, we weren’t seeing the consistent business needed to sustain the location.” 685 Manhattan Avenue, near Norman Avenue, Brooklyn Greenpoint : After a four-year run in Brooklyn’s cutthroat coffee corridor, tiny island-style cafe Kaleidoscope closed on Sunday, November 15. Per Greenpointers , co-owner Adam Stamper cites competition from places like Paloma the Bakery , which opened a short walk away in 2024, as well as the G train shutdowns as causes for the closure. The 310-square-foot shop specialized in cold brew, teas, matcha (gelato), cortados stamped with palm tree-shaped latte art, and affogato espressos. 151B Nassau Avenue, near Newel Street, Brooklyn Hudson: Suarez Family Brewery , the upstate NY mom-and-pop shop that makes pale ales of mixed fermentation, pale ales, and unfiltered lagers, will cease to operate “as you currently know it” on Sunday, November 22, per a statement to its followers. “Knowing that the current iteration has not been wholly sustainable for us,” the brewery says it will scale back production starting next year and only reopen its rustic-chic taproom to wholesale customers and the public for two weeks at a time each season, come spring, summer, and fall. items.text: Dining Reports Brasserie Boulud Is an Easy Answer Near Lincoln Center A patisserie, a speakeasy, and a dining room for everything from snacks to whole roast chicken by Melissa McCart Nov 18, 2026, 10:50 PM UTC Facebook Link A spread from Brasserie Boulud. Bill Milne/Brasserie Boulud Melissa McCart is the lead editor of the Northeast region with more than 20 years of experience as a reporter, critic, editor, and cookbook author. When Daniel Boulud closed Bar Boulud, Boulud Sud, and Épicerie Boulud across from Lincoln Center, the neighborhood lost a collection of places where people ate before the opera, after the movies, and at hours in between. In early October, he folded all three into Brasserie Boulud , a two-story, 10,000-square-foot brasserie at 1900 Broadway, at Lincoln Plaza. It’s hard to beat for convenience if you frequent the area: Épicerie Boulud handles coffee and pastries in the morning, and at night you can eat a snacky meal at the bar or stay for a full dinner. Chef Christina D’Angelo runs the kitchen, and the menu leans toward Boulud’s Lyon roots. The Rockwell Group–designed room is built around a big central bar, and ahead of the holiday season, it’s bustling with theatergoers, tourists, and Upper West Siders. The chicken from Brasserie Boulud. Bill Milne/Brasserie Boulud What to order Basque-style broiled topneck clams ($24) are a standout starter, their salinity balanced by a hint of heat from piquillo pepper and the sweetness of leeks. I enjoyed the savory saffron spaghetti ($29 as an appetizer) with the grated umami of bottarga and the faintly bitter dandelion greens. It also serves as a fine meal. For a group, get the poulet à la rôtisserie, a roasted Sasso chicken with tiny roasted potatoes, watercress, and garlic jus. A half is $39, and the whole bird is $76. The server’s gravy pour is immensely satisfying. If a burger is your thing, steer toward the classic ($25), a 6-ounce patty with cheddar, tomato, lettuce, and cornichon mayo that hits all the right notes. Since it comes with restaurant’s crisp fries, it’s a deal these days. End with the religieuse au praliné ($20), a throwback cream puff topped with caramelized hazelnuts. The drinks The wine list draws heavily from Burgundy and the Rhône, the regions closest to Boulud’s childhood home outside Lyon. Most wines by-the-glass are under $20. The bar and the speakeasy pour cocktails like a stiff Sidecar ($23) or an after-dinner Boulevardier ($20). Know before you go Brasserie Boulud is open Tuesday through Sunday, 4:30 p.m. to 10:30 p.m., and closed Mondays. Pre- and post-theater menus are back, so plan around curtain times at Lincoln Center. And Épicerie Boulud is open from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Insider tip The speakeasy serves the full menu, not just cocktails and bar snacks: Just ask. Daniel Boulud with Christina D’Angelo. items.text: LA Restaurant Openings Chef Charbel Hayek Brings a Casual Lebanese Cafe to Downtown Santa Monica ﻿Laya Café opens November 24 with Lebanese favorites and cocktails, one block from the Pacific by Mona Holmes Nov 20, 2026, 10:48 PM UTC Facebook Link Laya Café Mona Holmes is an editor at Eater Southern California/Southwest, a regular contributor at KCRW radio, and a 2022 James Beard Award nominee. In early December, chef Charbel Hayek will expand into Santa Monica with a casual restaurant, Laya Café . Over on the Westside, Hayek took over the former King & Queen Cantina, where an all-day menu fuses his Lebanese roots with a relaxed Los Angeles vibe. Since opening West Hollywood’s Ladyhawk in 2023, Hayek has been busy. In 2024, the Beirut-born winner of Top Chef: Middle East opened Laya on Cahuenga Boulevard in Hollywood, with authoritative Middle Eastern cooking and one of the most stunning patios in Los Angeles. In 2025, he opened Ilya, farther south in San Clemente. Now, Laya Café will provide a day-to-night dining option in Downtown Santa Monica, starting with Lebanese coffee, including a rose latte, along with fresh juices and baked goods such as a breakfast flatbread topped with haloumi and sumac. Hayek has designed a lunchtime menu of grab-and-go items (ideal for beachgoers, as the restaurant is one block from the Pacific Ocean), plus market items for home use; fast-casual service includes salads, a beef shawarma bowl, and a labneh sandwich with tomato, red onions, mint, za’atar, and olive oil, on Jyan Isaac sourdough. The shish tawouk packs thin saj flatbread with chicken cubes, romaine, pickled cucumber, and toum. Shifting to full service for dinner, Hayek’s team will offer starters like rakakat, deep-fried Lebanese phyllo rolls stuffed with cheese and herbs. Mains include grilled rockfish with a tahini mojo, herbs, and pomegranate molasses, and Levantine spaghetti bil laban, tossed with dried mint, brown butter, yogurt, and garlic. Laya Café’s full bar stays right on theme with a za’atar martini and a stunningly reasonable happy hour menu where wings, beef kabobs, and stuffed olives range from $4 to $8. When I first met Hayek in 2023, he brought fresh energy to Los Angeles. As prevalent as Middle Eastern cuisine is in the region, fine dining iterations remain fairly rare outside options like Bavel and Saffy’s . As someone whose job demands a lot of driving around, I will be stopping at Laya Café to wait out traffic, try something new, grab something to-go, watch the sunset in the 35-person dining room or on the 30-seat patio, and see more of what this innovative chef is up to. When it opens, Laya Café will open for lunch from 11 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., happy hour from 4 p.m. to 5:30 p.m., and dinner from 4 p.m. to 9 p.m. Tuesday to Sunday at 1401 Ocean Ave., Suite 104, Santa Monica, 90401. The over 8,000-square-foot restaurant property is listed at $12 million. Piscator NYC , New York’s viral fish pop-up, will return to Los Angeles for an extended residency. Owner Mason O’Avo did a brief SoCal stint in early 2026. Reservations go fast, so sign up for a spot between November and late March. It’s hard to imagine Los Angeles without Highland Park’s Joy or Pine & Crane . Food & Wine’s profile of owner Vivian Ku will leave readers with a thorough understanding of how her restaurants came to be. Are you as delighted as I am that the Original Pantry Cafe reopened? items.text: Dining Out in LA Your Los Angeles Restaurant Weekend Guide: November 20 Your handy guide on where to eat from the editors at Eater LA by Eater Staff Nov 20, 2026, 7:53 PM UTC Facebook Link Moo krata at Ayara Thai. | Ayara Thai Dining Out in LA Your Los Angeles Restaurant Weekend Guide: November 20 Your handy guide on where to eat from the editors at Eater LA by Eater Staff Nov 20, 2026, 7:53 PM UTC Facebook Link Moo krata at Ayara Thai. | Ayara Thai Facebook Link Every Friday, our editors compile a trusty list of recommendations to answer the most pressing of questions: “Where should I eat?” Here are four places to check out this weekend in Los Angeles. And if you need some ideas on where to drink, here’s our list of the hottest places to get cocktails in town. This week’s recommendations focus on the 2026 Eater Awards recipients in Los Angeles. For an attainable pre-Thanksgiving omakase in Beverly Hills: Sushi Note Omakase Sushi Note Omakase. Matthew Kang It had been a few years since I dined at the very cool subterranean expansion of Sushi Note, Sushi Note Omakase , tucked away by the valet station in the underground parking lot of a Rodeo Drive retail building otherwise known for its luxury watch shops. Chef Earl Aguilar remains at the counter, serving pristine fish with balanced shari (rice), and now he offers a $175 nigiri-only service of 12 different cuts ranging from bluefin tuna and shima aji (striped jack) to dry-aged Ora King salmon graced with edible flowers. The sushi here is pretty standard issue luxury edomae-style, which is great alongside the restaurant’s special feature: wine pairings, which make every course interesting. Recently, it’s become a bit of a celebrity haunt, with the likes of Leonardo DiCaprio coming through for a semi-secret sushi dinner. 421 N. Rodeo Drive, Beverly Hills, CA 90210. — Matthew Kang, correspondent, Eater For Indian food in the Valley: Flavor of India in Studio City Flavor of India. Rebecca Roland While running errands in the Valley the other week, I found myself with an all-consuming need for a crispy dosa. Realizing I was just a few minutes from Studio City standby Flavor of India, I redirected my evening toward the promise of naan and hot tea. The casual Valley restaurant serves a wide-ranging, well-executed menu of dishes such as aloo tikka, tandoori chicken, masala fries, and pani puri. But you also can’t go wrong with a potato-filled dosa, creamy tikka masala (legend has it, this was Dolly Parton’s favorite dish at the restaurant), and puffy garlic naan. If you’re headed over for lunch, check out the all-you-can-eat deal, served from 11:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. 12321 Ventura Boulevard, Studio City, CA 91604. — Rebecca Roland, deputy editor, Eater Southern California/Southwest For Thai hot pot available only this weekend: Ayara Thai in Westchester Moo krata at Ayara Thai. Ayara Thai I wish moo krata, or Thai-style hot pot, was more prevalent in Los Angeles because it is one of my favorite meals to have when in Thailand. For the uninitiated, moo krata (which translates to pork pan) is a combination barbecue and hot pot meal where the renderings of grilled ingredients spill into an accompanying moat of soup, enhancing the dish as the meal progresses. Ayara Thai in Westchester hosts semiannual moo krata nights. This weekend, the restaurant celebrates Loy Krathong, Thailand’s full moon lantern festival; you’ll need to book a special reservation for the moo krata experience. Available Friday night and Saturday night , the meal clocks in at $75 per person for a minimum of two guests. Expect a combination of proteins, from scallops to pork jowl to shaved ribeye, plenty of leafy vegetables, Thai-style sukiyaki sauce and spicy nam jim jaew, and a sweet coconut broth with glutinous rice dumplings for dessert. 6245 W. 87th Street, Los Angeles, CA 90045. — Kat Thompson, audience editor, Eater Southern California/Southwest For crispy katsu from a mom and pop spot in the Valley: Teriyaki Plus in Van Nuys Teriyaki Plus. Mona Holmes I always make it a point to visit casual Los Angeles restaurants that have staying power, especially those with minimal or no social media. Teriyaki Plus in Van Nuys was likely an OG Taco Bell in the 1970s — minimalist in interior style, but big on flavor. For less than $18, I walked out recently with a massive platter of katsu over rice, plus gyoza and a simple salad. I made it a point to get the miso soup for quick consumption, but this is easily a meal that can last two or three days. The mostly Japanese offerings come with a plethora of extras that are pure Los Angeles: egg rolls, kim chi, yakisoba, kebabs. As I walked away with my heavily packed styrofoam container, the incredibly friendly kitchen staff yelled “Thanks for coming!” Next time, I’ll come with a group and order a ton while sitting in the dining room overlooking a busy stretch of Sepulveda Boulevard. 7312 Sepulveda Boulevard, Van Nuys, CA, 91405. — Mona Holmes, editor, Eater Southern California/Southwest Related The 38 Best Restaurants in Los Angeles See More : Dining Out in LA Dining Out

items.text: Eater Archives Where to Eat at Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) How and what to eat when traveling out of Southern California’s busy airport by Eater Staff Updated Nov 20, 2026, 6:15 PM UTC Facebook Link If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. LAX. Getty Images Traveling through Los Angeles International Airport can sometimes be a nightmare, with traffic into the airport, inefficient security lines, and unplanned delays. Since 2019, LAX has been busy with construction and renovations , including a highly anticipated but delayed people mover , which means significant changes for the restaurants, lounges, and bars at the airport. With years of construction already completed, the Los Angeles International Airport looks better than ever for passenger experiences inside the terminals. And travelers will be thrilled to eventually see the opening of the long-delayed Automated People Mover , whisking passengers to and from rental car lots, parking lots, rideshare, and public transit. Here is an updated look, just ahead of the winter travel season, and what to expect when seeking out food at Los Angeles’s busy airport. The Eater Guide to LA $ 20 $ 20 From home to Hollywood, Eater’s got you covered. Read More $20 at Amazon $20 at Bookshop Five Standout Places to Eat Kogi BBQ in Terminal 1: An outpost of Roy Choi’s Kogi BBQ is now operating out of Terminal 1, serving Korean barbecue short rib, spicy gochujang-marinated pork, sweet garlic teriyaki chicken, and tofu in tacos and burritos. Native by Nyesha, a restaurant by Nyesha Arrington at LAX’s Terminal 3. Matthew Kang Native by Nyesha at Terminal 3: A resurrected version of chef Nyesha Arrington’s former Santa Monica restaurant , the current Eater YouTube host has a globally-inspired spot in Terminal 3 with green curry corn chowder, avocado toast, salmon rice bowl, and a fried chicken sandwich with hot curry mustard in what might be the most ambitious chef-driven restaurant in the entire airport. The beet salad with goat cheese, citrus, pistachios, chicken, and sherry vinaigrette is a good way to have a tasty pre-flight meal without feeling too full. The service is also speedy, with most dishes coming out in rapid succession. The Kitchen by Wolfgang Puck at LAX’s Terminal 6. Matthew Kang WPizza and The Kitchen by Wolfgang Puck at Terminal 6 and Tom Bradley International Terminal: Celebrity chef Wolfgang Puck’s classic pizzas, pasta, and salads are often the most reliable things to eat in an airport setting, though the prices will certainly be higher than in a fast food spot. Expect better-than-average pizza that keeps well in case hunger strikes mid-flight. Beecher’s Handmade Cheese stall at Tom Bradley International Terminal. LAX Shop & Dine Beecher’s Handmade Cheese at Tom Bradley International Terminal: The Seattle-based cheese shop offers breakfast sandwiches, soup, and grilled cheese sandwiches at reasonable prices. Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse at LAX. Virgin Atlantic The Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse is a lounge that’s available to Priority Pass holders (which is included with multiple credit cards like Chase Sapphire Reserve and Capital One Venture X) inside Tom Bradley International Terminal. Access to the lounge does cost an additional $35 per-person “top-up” fee, but offers one of the best selections of food and drink in the entire airport. From lunch through dinner, there’s a wide menu of dishes made to order, including sticky Korean chicken wings, tuna poke bowls, and miso doughnuts, plus a venison smash burger and fish and chips. The drinks menu is also dizzying, with full espresso, tea, cocktails, wine, juices, and spirits. The small but comfortable lounge does fill up during prime hours, so be prepared to wait or go as early as possible. Note : The breakfast options aren’t as ample as the food served later in the day, so it’s ideal to arrive after 11:30 a.m. Urth Caffe and Bar at LAX’s Terminal 1. Matthew Kang Terminal 1 A Quick Meal California Pizza Kitchen: California-style pizza, sandwiches, salads, and appetizers The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf: Coffee, blended drinks, and baked goods Chick-fil-A: Southern-style fried chicken sandwiches, waffle fries, and sweet tea Einstein Bros.
